Learning curve

Warm up level:

  1. Develop skills in programming (my advice for beginners will be Python), learn about mechanical assembling and electronics.
  • Corey Schafer’s Python for Beginners Playlist
  1. Implement the knowledge on a micro-controller unit (popular choice is Arduino).
  • Exploring Arduino: Tools & Techniques for Engineering Wizardry

This is not ideally robotics but it lays a good foundation for one to further advance in the field.

Beginner level:

  1. Learn object-oriented programming (OOP), data structures, and basic algorithms.
  • Data Structures and Algorithms with Python
  • Data Structures & Other Objects using C++

(There is also a book by the same author for Java.)

  • Introduction to Algorithms
  1. Familiarize yourself with Linux operating system.
  • LINUX: Easy Linux For Beginners
  1. Learn more maths, physics, linear algebra, and probability.
  • Khan Academy Playlists for each
  1. With better knowledge of coding, circuitry, theoretical concepts, and familiarity with Linux, implement these on a smaller computer -Raspberry Pi or the BeagleBone.
  • Make a Raspberry Pi-Controlled Robot: Building a Rover with Python, Linux, Motors, and Sensors

Intermediate level:

Learn about more advanced theoretical concepts.

  1. Introduction to Robotics: Mechanics, Planning, and Control
  • Probabilistic Robotics
  • Adrian Rosebrock’s course on Computer Vision
  • Python: Machine Learning
  1. Familiarize yourself with Robot Operating System
  • Programming Robots with ROS
  • Mastering ROS for Robotics Programming

Books

https://github.com/manjunath5496/Robotics-Books/tree/master

"Robot Building for Beginners" by David Cook: This book is a great starting point for beginners and covers the basics of robot building using inexpensive materials and simple tools. "Robotics: Everything You Need to Know About Robotics from Beginner to Expert" by Peter Mckinnon: This book provides a comprehensive overview of robotics, starting from the basics and progressing to more advanced concepts. "Make: Electronics: Learning Through Discovery" by Charles Platt: While not solely focused on robotics, this book provides a solid foundation in electronics, which is essential for understanding and building robots. "Arduino Robotics" by Warren, John-David: This book focuses on using Arduino microcontrollers to build robots and is a good resource for beginners interested in programming and electronics. "Learning Robotics Using Python" by Lentin Joseph: This book introduces robotics concepts using the Python programming language, making it a great choice for beginners with some programming experience.
